extraction.name: TextVQA
extraction.description: A dataset for visual question answering containing questions that require reading and reasoning about text in images.
extraction.creator: Amanpreet Singh, Vivek Natarajan, Meet Shah, Yu Jiang, Xinlei Chen, Dhruv Batra, Devi Parikh, Marcus Rohrbach
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were sourced from Open Images v3, with categories likely to contain text identified using OCR statistics. A three-stage crowdsourcing pipeline was used: annotators first filtered out images without text, then collected 1-2 questions per image requiring reading text, and finally collected 10 answers per question with quality-control flags and bad-annotator filtering.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Some images had no OCR tokens detected by the OCR system despite containing text.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images from the Open Images v3 dataset, especially categories tending to contain text such as billboard, traffic sign, and whiteboard.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Categories were sampled based on normalized average OCR box counts computed from random images per category; images without text and noisy annotations were filtered out; questions flagged by a majority as invalid or unanswerable were removed; bad annotators were identified using hand-crafted questions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: OCR was run on sampled images to estimate text-rich categories; images without text were filtered; invalid questions were removed based on majority worker flags; OCR tokens were analyzed and manually verified in some zero-token cases.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers first marked whether images contained text, then wrote 1-2 questions per image that required reading text to answer, and finally provided 10 answers per question. Annotators were instructed that questions must require reading text, and quality-control options allowed flagging no-text, non-question, no-reading-required, or unanswerable items.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Questions were removed when a majority of workers flagged them as invalid. Agreement statistics were reported for answers, with all 10 annotators agreeing on 22.8% of questions and at least 3 annotators agreeing on 97.9% of questions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset targets an important assistive use case for visually impaired users, since many real-world questions they ask involve reading text in images.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset appears to have limited question/image shortcut bias according to reported baselines, but it is constructed from categories likely to contain text and most questions start with 'what'.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The OCR system is imperfect and fails on rotated, unstructured, or partially occluded text. Some questions require combining multiple OCR tokens, which the model does not handle. The dataset is built from text-rich image categories, and OCR sometimes returns zero tokens for images that do contain text.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and training/evaluating VQA models that can read and reason about text in images.

name.evidence: First, we introduce a new “TextVQA” dataset to facilitate progress on this important problem.

description.evidence: We introduce the TextVQA dataset. It contains 45,336 questions asked by (sighted) humans on 28,408 images from the Open Images dataset [27] from categories that tend to contain text e.g. “billboard”, “traffic sign”, “whiteboard”. Questions in the dataset require reading and reasoning about text in the image.

creator.evidence: Towards VQA Models That Can Read Amanpreet Singh1, Vivek Natarajan, Meet Shah1, Yu Jiang1, Xinlei Chen1, Dhruv Batra1,2, Devi Parikh1,2, Marcus Rohrbach1

isLiveDataset.evidence: We divide TextVQA into train, validation and test splits with size 34,602, 5,000, and 5,734, respectively.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We use Open Images v3 dataset [27] as the source of our images... We set up a three stage pipeline for crowd-sourcing our data. In the first stage, annotators were asked to identify images that did not contain text (using a forced-choice “yes”/“no” flag). Filtering those (and noisy data from annotators) out resulted in 28,408 images, which form the basis of our TextVQA dataset. In the second stage, we collect 1-2 questions for each image... Following VQA [3, 10] and VizWiz [13] datasets, we collect 10 answers for each question.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We use Open Images v3 dataset [27] as the source of our images... We run a state-of-the-art OCR model Rosetta [6] on these images and compute the average number of OCR boxes in a category... We set up a three stage pipeline for crowd-sourcing our data.

rai:dataCollectionMissingData.evidence: In some cases, when the system is unable to detect text we get 0 tokens but those cases are restricted to ∼1.5k images and we manually verified that the images actually do contain text.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We use Open Images v3 dataset [27] as the source of our images... Several categories in Open Images fit this criterion (e.g., billboard, traffic sign, whiteboard).

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: We run a state-of-the-art OCR model Rosetta [6] on these images and compute the average number of OCR boxes in a category. The average number of OCR boxes per-category were normalized and used as per-category weights for sampling the images from the categories... Filtering those (and noisy data from annotators) out resulted in 28,408 images... We remove the questions where a majority of workers marked any of these flags. Additionally, we use hand-crafted questions for which we know the correct answers to identify and filter out bad annotators.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: To automate this process of identifying categories that tend to have images with text in them, we select 100 random images from each category... We run a state-of-the-art OCR model Rosetta [6] on these images... In the first stage, annotators were asked to identify images that did not contain text... We remove the questions where a majority of workers marked any of these flags... In some cases, when the system is unable to detect text we get 0 tokens but those cases are restricted to ∼1.5k images and we manually verified that the images actually do contain text.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: In the first stage, annotators were asked to identify images that did not contain text (using a forced-choice “yes”/“no” flag)... In the second stage, we collect 1-2 questions for each image... Specifically, they were told to ‘Please ensure that answering the question requires reading of the text in the image. It is OK if the answer cannot be directly copied from the text but needs to be inferred or paraphrased.’... Following VQA [3, 10] and VizWiz [13] datasets, we collect 10 answers for each question... we give annotators these four options: (i) no text in image; (ii) not a question; (iii) answering the question doesn’t require reading any text in image; and (iv) unanswerable

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: We remove the questions where a majority of workers marked any of these flags... All 10 annotators agree on the most common answer for 22.8% questions, while 3 or more annotators agree on most common answer for 97.9% questions.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: Each question-image pair has 10 ground truth answers provided by humans.

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: It contains 45,336 questions asked by (sighted) humans on 28,408 images

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: For OCR, we run the Rosetta OCR system [6] to provide us word strings s1; :::; s N.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Studies have shown that a dominant class of questions asked by visually impaired users on images of their surroundings involves reading text in the image... Specifically, the VizWiz study [5] found that up to 21% of these questions involve reading and reasoning about the text captured in the images of a user’s surroundings

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Question only (Q) and Image only (I) baseline get 8.09% and 6.29% validation accuracies, respectively, which shows that the dataset does not have significant biases w.r.t. images and questions... We also observe that most questions start with “what”

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Our OCR model, while mature, still fails at detecting text that is rotated, a bit unstructured (e.g., a scribble) or partially occluded... Note that if the model chooses to copy, it can only produce one of the OCR tokens as the predicted answer. 8.9% of the TextVQA questions can only be answered by combining multiple OCR tokens; we leave this as future work... In some cases, when the system is unable to detect text we get 0 tokens but those cases are restricted to ∼1.5k images and we manually verified that the images actually do contain text.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: First, we introduce a new “TextVQA” dataset to facilitate progress on this important problem... We find that the gap between human performance and machine performance is significantly larger on TextVQA than on VQA 2.0, suggesting that TextVQA is well-suited to benchmark progress along directions complementary to VQA 2.0.
